By the [[Time/Legends|time]] of the [[Jedi Civil War]] fought between the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] and the [[Darth Revan's Sith Empire|Sith Empire]], a '''smuggling ring''' had been run by a [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggler]] named [[Galduran Calrissian]] in the region of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] known as [[Hutt Space/Legends|Hutt Space]].<ref name="kotor" /> By the [[Standard year/Legends|year]] [[3956 BBY]],<ref name="KotORDate" /> the organization had made Calrissian's name infamous, because the ring was not sanctioned by the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutts]],<ref name="kotor" /> the [[Species/Legends|species]] who controlled Hutt [[Realspace/Legends|Space]].<ref name="NEGAS">''[[The New Essential Guide to Alien Species]]''</ref> The infamy eventually placed Calrissian in a situation in which [[Gender/Legends|he]] was forced to sell his personal effects, including his [[Calrissian's utility belt|utility belt]], to keep from becoming the last of the Calrissian line.<ref name="kotor" />

==Behind the scenes==
Galduran Calrissian's smuggling ring was first mentioned in ''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic]]'', a [[2003]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] produced by [[BioWare]]. The ring was briefly mentioned in the game through the description for Calrissian's [[Belt/Legends|belt]], which was a unique item that the player could purchase from [[Crattis Yurkal]] on [[Dantooine/Legends|Dantooine]]. However, the item description did not specify the fate of Calrissian's smuggling ring.<ref name="kotor" /> An entry on the belt, which did not mention the smuggling ring, was included in [[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic: Prima's Official Strategy Guide|''Star Wars Knights of the Old Republic'': Prima's Official Strategy Guide]] by [[Prima Games]] and spelled Calrissian's first name "Garduran."<ref name="kotorsg">[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic: Prima's Official Strategy Guide|''Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic'': Prima's Official Strategy Guide]]</ref> This article was written with the assumption that the spelling in the game was correct.
